description: The bar chart illustrates the distribution of narrative roles—HERO, VICTIM, and VILLAIN—across four media bias categories: Left bias, Left center bias, Right bias, and an unlabeled category marked as “source” (represented by a gray square beneath the x-axis). The vertical axis is scaled from 0.0 to 1.0, representing the normalized proportion of each role within each bias category. Each bar is a stacked column, with HERO shown in dark blue at the bottom, VICTIM in brown in the middle, and VILLAIN in light blue at the top. In “Left bias,” HERO accounts for approximately 0.32, VICTIM for 0.14, and VILLAIN for 0.54. In “Left center bias,” HERO is about 0.35, VICTIM is 0.20, and VILLAIN is 0.45. The “source” category is not visually represented as a stacked bar, suggesting it may be a placeholder or omitted data point. In “Right bias,” HERO is approximately 0.26, VICTIM is 0.14, and VILLAIN is 0.60. The chart visually emphasizes that VILLAIN is the dominant role across all bias categories, with the highest proportion in Right bias and the lowest in Left center bias, while HERO is consistently the second-largest segment except in Right bias, where it is smaller than in other categories. The bars are arranged left to right in the order of bias categories, with no apparent sorting by total height or role proportion.
